title: Bulletproof Cannabis Coffee with Canna-Coconut Oil
h1: Bulletproof Cannabis Coffee, Dosed Your Way
metaDescription: Blend a butter coffee with a small, adjustable spoon of canna-coconut oil or infused ghee, with tips for blending hot coffee safely and not overdoing it.
excerpt: A five-minute butter coffee where only part of the fat is infused, so you learn your dose before you scale up.
keyTakeaways: Swap only part of the fat for canna-coconut oil or infused ghee, starting at 1/8 to 1/4 teaspoon.
THC in food can need 2 hours to register and lingers for hours, so make this a day-off drink.
Hot coffee builds steam in a blender: fill it halfway at most, vent it the way your manual says and start slow.
In the first controlled human study of the pair (2025), caffeine barely changed how THC felt.
body:
Cannabis coffee in the bulletproof style is hot coffee blended with butter or ghee and coconut oil until creamy and foamy. THC dissolves in fat, so a measured spoon of canna-coconut oil or infused ghee blends right in, while the rest of the fat stays plain to keep the dose small.

## Dosing and safety: start small, plan a slow day

If your canna-coconut oil works out to about 13 mg per teaspoon at most, a quarter teaspoon carries about 3 mg and an eighth about 1.6 mg. Infused food can take as long as 2 hours to register, and its effects can linger 4 to 12 hours, so a morning cup shapes your whole day. Make it a day-off drink, never one before work or driving. Our [THC dosage guide](/blog/thc-dosage-guide/) walks through first doses.

## What goes in cannabis coffee

Most of the fat is plain: a tablespoon of unsalted butter or ghee and a teaspoon or two of coconut or MCT oil. The infused part is just 1/8 to 1/4 teaspoon of canna-coconut oil or infused ghee, from our [cannabutter recipe](/blog/canna-butter-recipe/) or [canna oil recipe](/blog/canna-oil-recipe/). Measure it with a real measuring spoon, and add a pinch of salt.

## How to blend hot coffee safely

Warm the blender jar with hot tap water first. Fill it no more than halfway, since steam can push hot liquid past the lid, and vent the lid the way your blender's manual says for hot liquids. Hold a folded towel over the lid, start on the lowest speed, then raise it and blend for about 20 seconds, until foamy. A milk frother in a tall mug works too.

## Storage and labeling

Drink it right away, before it separates and before anyone else can grab an infused cup. Keep the infused oil labeled with its strength and date, apart from the plain oil and out of children's and pets' reach. Homemade oils made with herbs belong in the fridge for no more than 4 days, so freeze small portions of what you won't use by then.

## Variations

- **Dairy-free:** plain coconut oil in place of the butter, with canna-coconut oil rather than infused ghee.
- **Iced:** blend with room-temperature coffee, then pour over ice.
- **Spiced:** a pinch of cinnamon and a drop of vanilla.
- **Sweet:** maple syrup, or [canna-honey](/blog/canna-honey/) with all-plain oils.

For a cold, fruity option, try our [cannabis smoothie recipe](/blog/cannabis-smoothie-recipe/).

faq.q: How much canna-oil should go in coffee?
faq.a: An eighth to a quarter teaspoon. With oil at about 13 mg per teaspoon at most, a quarter teaspoon is roughly 3 mg. Canada's chief medical officers of health set 2.5 mg as a sensible ceiling for a first edible, so an eighth is the cautious start.

faq.q: Does caffeine change how THC feels?
faq.a: Not much, according to the first controlled human study of the pair. In a 2025 Johns Hopkins trial with 20 adults, adding about 180 mg of caffeine to 7.5 mg of oral THC barely changed THC's effects, impairment or blood levels. It may have shifted how impaired people felt behind the wheel, and it won't cancel out THC.

faq.q: Can I use cannabutter instead of coconut oil?
faq.a: Yes. Butter coffee already calls for butter, so swapping part of it for cannabutter or infused ghee works the same way. Measure the infused portion by the teaspoon and keep the rest of the fat plain, so the dose stays small.

sources.label: Strickland J.C. et al., Effect of caffeine and cannabidiol co-administration on THC subjective effects, performance impairment and pharmacokinetics, Neuropsychopharmacology (2025)
Public Health Agency of Canada: Council of Chief Medical Officers of Health statement on cannabis extracts, edibles and topicals (2020)
CDC: Botulism Prevention (homemade oils made with garlic or herbs)
University of Georgia Extension, Circular 1334: How to Safely Make Infused Oils (2024)

ingredients: 1 to 2 teaspoons plain coconut or MCT oil
1/8 to 1/4 teaspoon canna-coconut oil or infused ghee (see the note)
steps: Warm the blender jar with hot tap water, then pour the water out.
Add the coffee, butter or ghee, plain oil, measured infused oil and salt, filling the jar no more than halfway.
Set the lid the way your blender's manual says for hot liquids, hold a folded towel over it and start on the lowest speed.
Raise the speed gradually and blend for about 20 seconds, until creamy and foamy. Drink it right away.
recipe.dosingNote: Estimate only: if your canna-coconut oil comes to about 13 mg per teaspoon, a quarter teaspoon is roughly 3 mg and an eighth roughly 1.6 mg. How strong your oil really is comes down to the starting flower and the losses from decarbing and infusing. Begin at the low end and let at least 2 hours go by before another cup. The oil jar needs a clear label and a spot kids and pets can't reach.

claims.claim: THC dissolves in fat, so infused oil blends into butter coffee
claims.source: PubChem CID 16078 (PUG View, Solubility): 'Essentially insoluble in water', 'Soluble in fixed oils'. Read 2026-10-24.

claims.claim: At about 13 mg per teaspoon, a quarter teaspoon is about 3 mg and an eighth about 1.5 mg (body and dosing note)
claims.fix: 13/4 = 3.25 (about 3, kept); 13/8 = 1.625, so 'about 1.5' became 'about 1.6' in both places.
claims.source: Arithmetic. 13 mg/tsp is stated as a conditional ('if your oil works out to'), matching the full-cup figure of the canna-butter-recipe worksheet.

claims.claim: Infused food can take up to 2 hours to register; effects can linger 4 to 12 hours
claims.source: CCMOH statement, Public Health Agency of Canada (Jan. 6, 2020), opened 2026-10-24.

claims.claim: Dosing note: let 2 hours go by before another cup
claims.fix: Now 'at least 2 hours': the same statement says full effects can take up to 4 hours.
claims.source: CCMOH 2020: 'up to 4 hours to feel the full effects'.

claims.claim: Canada's chief medical officers of health set 2.5 mg as a sensible ceiling for a first edible (FAQ)
claims.source: CCMOH 2020: 'Start with small amounts - 2.5 mg of THC or less for products that you eat or drink.'

claims.claim: In 'the one controlled human study so far' caffeine barely changed how THC felt (takeaway and FAQ)
claims.fix: The paper calls itself 'the first direct assessment' (Sept. 2025); whether it is still the only one in October 2026 was not established. Now 'the first controlled human study of the pair (2025)'.
claims.source: Strickland 2025 abstract via NCBI E-utilities (PMID 40962814), read 2026-10-24.

claims.claim: 2025 Johns Hopkins trial, 20 adults, about 180 mg caffeine with 7.5 mg oral THC barely changed THC's effects, impairment or blood levels; may have shifted perceived driving impairment; does not cancel out THC
claims.source: Strickland 2025 abstract: Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine; N = 20; oral THC 7.5 mg cumulative, caffeine 180 mg cumulative; 'minimal changes in THC-induced subjective effects, performance, or metabolism, although signals for perceived driving impairment were observed'.

claims.claim: Blender: 'hot liquid expands as it blends'; lift out the lid's center cap; 'pulse a few times' (body, takeaway, recipe step)
claims.fix: Manuals differ and one forbids both steps: the DeLonghi AT358 manual says hot liquid and steam can be forced past the lid, to start at low speed, 'NEVER blend hot liquids by using the Pulse setting', and to run only with the vented filler cap in place. Now: fill halfway at most, vent the lid as the blender's manual says, towel over the lid, start on the lowest speed and raise it gradually; no pulsing.
claims.source: DeLonghi AT358 instructions, https://dls.delonghigroup.com/files/docs/5/at358%20ib%20usca.pdf (text extracted 2026-10-24). Half-full limit is common guidance; manuals set their own limits.

claims.claim: Homemade infused oils keep 4 days in the fridge
claims.fix: Kept, reworded to the CDC's terms (oils made with herbs), and added freezing for what won't be used in 4 days; UGA source added.
claims.source: CDC Botulism Prevention (Feb. 26, 2026): 'Refrigerate homemade oils made with garlic or herbs. Throw the oils away after 4 days.' UGA Extension C1334 (Dec. 17, 2024): 'discarded 4 days after being made... Alternatively, you could freeze the oil'.

claims.claim: Dairy-free variation: plain coconut oil in place of the butter
claims.fix: It is dairy-free only if the infused part is too; now 'with canna-coconut oil rather than infused ghee'.
claims.source: Recipe logic: the infused part may be infused ghee, a dairy fat.

claims.claim: Make it a day-off drink, never before work or driving
Recipe quantities (1 tbsp butter or ghee, 1-2 tsp coconut or MCT oil, 1/8-1/4 tsp infused oil), canna-honey only with all-plain oils, drink before it separates
claims.source: Culinary method; the one-infused-ingredient rule keeps the dose countable.
None stated; no shop, menu, deals or rewards links.

review.factCheckNotes: Fact-check 2026-10-24: 13 claims checked, 5 fixed (eighth-teaspoon math, 'only study' claim, blender pulse and venting steps, wait time, dairy-free variation); the 4-day oil rule was ok and gained a freezing option. 'Bulletproof' stays as the generic style name the brief chose; no company or product is named.
review.writerNotes: No keto, weight-loss or energy claims; framed as a day-off drink, never before work or driving (mustAvoid). "Bulletproof" is used as the common style name in the title and h1 per the brief; no product or company is named. Blender safety advice is general kitchen practice.
